questions.question: Who is the Administrative Head of the Indian Audit and Accounts Department?
questions.solution:
The Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) of India is the Administrative Head of the Indian Audit and Accounts Department. As per Article 148 of the Constitution, the CAG is appointed by the President and is responsible for auditing all receipts and expenditures of the Government of India and the State Governments.

Note: The CAG is often called the 'Guardian of the Public Purse'.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution are related to citizenship?
questions.solution:
Articles 5 to 11 under Part II of the Indian Constitution deal with Citizenship. These articles provide for citizenship at the commencement of the Constitution and empower the Parliament to regulate the right of citizenship by law.

Additional Info: The Citizenship Act of 1955 was enacted by Parliament based on the powers given in Article 11.

questions.question: Which of the following options conveys the meaning of the word ‘Republic’ in the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution:
In the Indian Constitution, the word 'Republic' signifies that India has an Elected head of state rather than a hereditary monarch. The President of India is the head of state and is elected indirectly for a fixed tenure.

Key Concept: This means all public offices are open to every citizen without any discrimination.

questions.question: KA Najeeb Vs Union of India case deals with violation of rights under____________.
questions.solution:
The KA Najeeb Vs Union of India case is a landmark judgment involving Article 21 (Right to Life and Personal Liberty). The Supreme Court held that the constitutional courts can grant bail to an accused under the UAPA if the right to a speedy trial is being violated.

Note: It emphasizes that fundamental rights cannot be superseded by statutory restrictions like Section 43D(5) of the UAPA.

questions.question: Who holds the authority of transferring judges from one High court to another High Court?
questions.option_1: The senior most judge of Supreme Court
questions.solution:
The President of India holds the authority to transfer judges from one High Court to another. According to Article 222, the President can exercise this power after consultation with the Chief Justice of India (CJI).

Note: The CJI's opinion in this matter is usually based on a 'collegium' of senior judges.

questions.question: The Fundamental Duties were added to the Constitution of India by the ____ Amendment.
questions.solution:
The Fundamental Duties were added to the Constitution of India by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976. This amendment inserted Part IV-A and Article 51A into the Constitution.

Additional Info: Initially, 10 duties were added; the 11th was added later by the 86th Amendment in 2002.

questions.question: When was the Secretary of State for India made responsible for the Government of British India by bringing about changes in the Home Government?
questions.solution:
The Secretary of State for India was made responsible for the Government of British India in 1858 through the Government of India Act 1858. This followed the Revolt of 1857, leading to the end of Company Rule and the start of the British Raj (Crown Rule).

Note: The Secretary of State was a member of the British Cabinet.

questions.question: Who is the first law officer of India?
questions.solution:
The Attorney General of India is the first law officer of the country. Appointed by the President under Article 76, they give legal advice to the Government of India and represent it in the Supreme Court.

Note: They have the right to speak in both Houses of Parliament but do not have the right to vote.

questions.question: Which Constitutional Amendment added Fundamental Duties in the Constitution?
questions.solution: The Forty-Second Amendment Act, 1976 added the Fundamental Duties to the Indian Constitution. These were incorporated based on the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee to remind citizens of their social obligations while enjoying fundamental rights.

questions.question: When did the Drafting Committee publish the first draft of the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution:
The Drafting Committee, headed by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, published the first draft of the Indian Constitution in February 1948. The people of India were given eight months to discuss the draft and propose amendments.

Note: The final version was adopted on 26th November 1949.

questions.question: On 20 July 2021, the Supreme Court struck down certain provisions of part IX B of the Constitution of India. Part IX B was related to:
questions.solution:
In July 2021, the Supreme Court struck down provisions of Part IX B, which related to Co-operative Societies. The court held that the 97th Amendment required ratification by half of the states because it dealt with 'Co-operative Societies', which is a State Subject.

Note: Part IX covers Panchayats and Part IX A covers Municipalities.

questions.question: Which part of the Constitution of India contains the provisions of Union Executive?
questions.solution:
Part V of the Constitution contains provisions regarding the Union Executive (Articles 52 to 78). This includes the President, Vice-President, Prime Minister, Council of Ministers, and the Attorney General.

Hierarchy: Part III deals with Fundamental Rights, Part IV with DPSP, and Part VI with the States.

questions.question: Which of the following amendments to the Indian Constitution made the Right to Property a Legal Right in place of a Fundamental Right?
questions.solution: The 44th Amendment Act, 1978 removed the Right to Property from the list of Fundamental Rights and made it a Legal Right under Article 300A. This was done to ensure that the state could acquire land for public welfare without being hindered by fundamental right litigations.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution provides for a bicameral Parliament of India?
questions.solution:
Article 79 provides for the constitution of a bicameral Parliament consisting of the President and two Houses: the Council of States (Rajya Sabha) and the House of the People (Lok Sabha).

Additional Info: Article 80 and 81 define the composition of the Rajya Sabha and Lok Sabha respectively.

questions.question: Fundamental duties were not placed in Part III of the Indian Constitution because Part III is ____________.
questions.solution: Fundamental Duties are not in Part III because Part III is justiciable (enforceable by courts). Since Fundamental Duties are non-justiciable (moral obligations that cannot be enforced through legal action), they were placed in a separate part (Part IV-A).

questions.question: On 28 June 2021, the Supreme Court held that persons with disabilities have a right to reservation in promotion under Article 16(4) of the Constitution of India, 1950, in the case of:
questions.option_1: Indra Sawhney v. Union of India
questions.option_2: State of Kerala v. Leesamma Joseph
questions.option_4: State of Kerala v. N.M. Thomas
questions.solution: The case of State of Kerala v. Leesamma Joseph (2021) confirmed that persons with disabilities (PwDs) have a right to reservation in promotions. The Supreme Court clarified that Article 16(4) allows for this to ensure equal opportunity and participation in public employment.

questions.question: The Fundamental Duties of citizens were added to the Constitution of India, upon the recommendations of which of the following committees?
questions.solution:
The Swaran Singh Committee (1976) recommended the inclusion of Fundamental Duties. The committee suggested that while the Constitution provides rights, it should also prescribe certain duties for citizens to follow toward the nation.

Note: Santhanam Committee is related to anti-corruption (CVC).

questions.question:
Which of the following statements are correct regarding the Centre-State Relations pertaining to the three lists of the Indian Constitution?
A.The subjects which are not included in any of the three lists are called Residuary subjects.
B.If there is any conflict between the Union List and the State List, then the former prevails.
C.When the Parliament enacts a law on the request of two or more states, then that law made by the Parliament on the State List is applicable to all the states.
questions.solution:
Statement A and B only are correct. Residuary subjects (A) are those not in any list, and the Union List prevails (B) over the State List in case of conflict. Statement C is incorrect because a law made by Parliament at the request of specific states applies only to those states, unless others adopt it later.

Note: These relations are defined in Article 246.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements are correct regarding the Union Public Service Commission?
A. The Parliament has the power to make regulations as to conditions of service of the Chairman, members and staff of the commission.
B. The Government of India Act, 1935, envisaged a Public Service Commission for the Federation and a Provincial Public Service Commission for each Province or group of Provinces.
C. The Federal Public Service Commission came to be known as the Union Public Service Commission by virtue of Clause (1) of Article 378 of the Constitution in 1950.
questions.solution: Statements B and C only are correct. The 1935 Act (B) did create the Federal and Provincial PSCs, and the Federal PSC became the UPSC (C) in 1950. Statement A is incorrect because the President, not Parliament, has the power to make regulations regarding the conditions of service for members.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution talks about ‘abolition of title’?
questions.solution:
Article 18 of the Indian Constitution mandates the abolition of titles. It prohibits the State from conferring any title (except military or academic) and forbids Indian citizens from accepting titles from foreign states.

Note: This ensures social equality; Article 17 deals with the abolition of untouchability.

questions.question: In India The State election Commissioner is appointed by the _________ .
questions.solution: The Governor of the state appoints the State Election Commissioner. While the SEC is responsible for conducting elections for local bodies like Panchayats and Municipalities, their removal process is similar to that of a High Court Judge to ensure independence.

questions.question: According to Article _________of the Constitution of India, it shall be the duty of every citizen of India to develop the scientific temper, humanism and the spirit of inquiry and reform.
questions.solution:
Article 51A defines the Fundamental Duties of Indian citizens. Specifically, Clause (h) states that it is the duty of every citizen to 'develop the scientific temper, humanism and the spirit of inquiry and reform'.

Note: These duties serve as a reminder of civic responsibility.

questions.question: The origin of Directive Principles of State Policy can be traced to which of the following?
questions.solution:
The Karachi Resolution (1931) of the Indian National Congress is considered a precursor to the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP). It outlined a programme for social and economic rights, which later influenced the Drafting Committee.

Note: The DPSP were also inspired by the Irish Constitution.

questions.question: The total number of Ministers, including the Chief Minister, in the Council of Ministers in a State shall NOT exceed ________ of the total number of members of the Legislative Assembly of that State.
questions.solution:
According to the 91st Amendment Act, 2003, the total number of Ministers in a State cannot exceed 15 percent of the total strength of the Legislative Assembly. However, the number of ministers, including the CM, shall not be less than 12.

Purpose: To prevent jumbo cabinets and political instability.

questions.question:
Which of the following pairs is/are correctly matched regarding the terminology used in the Parliament?
A. Appropriation Bill — A Money Bill passed for providing for the withdrawal or appropriation from and out of the Consolidated Fund of India
B. Demand for Grants — Earmarking of budgetary allocation for meeting only planned expenditure of a Ministry/Department
C. Short Duration Discussion — For raising a discussion on a matter of urgent public importance for which a notice has to be given by a Member and supported by 50 Members
questions.solution: Statement A only is correct. An Appropriation Bill is indeed a Money Bill for withdrawing funds from the Consolidated Fund. Demand for Grants (B) covers both planned and non-planned expenditure. Short Duration Discussion (C) requires a notice but not specifically 50 supporting members (that is often required for Adjournment motions).
